meal.title: Why a blocked process must become ready first
meal.objective: Explain why a blocked process must become ready before it can run

voice.script: Why can’t a blocked process jump straight to running? A process moves through defined states. A state transition is simply the change from one condition to another. When a process is blocked, it is waiting for some event, like input or a lock. It cannot run because the needed resource isn’t available. Once that event occurs, the operating system marks the process as ready, placing it in the queue of processes that can run. Only processes in the ready state are eligible to be scheduled onto the CPU, so the blocked one must become ready before it can run. Here’s the flow of states.
